provenance.note: Every claim on this site resolves to a specific commit and, where the claim is a measurement, to a specific green build of that commit. The hashes below are the ones the site was built from.

checks.claim: CI Kit is published, open source, and MIT licensed

checks.claim: The performance numbers are reproducible, not asserted

documents.item: Published repositories and their commit history

record.statement: This page collects, in one place, the public record of my work: published software with measured outcomes, a published account of how those measurements were taken, and long-form writing on specific technical subjects. Every entry links to the artefact that supports it, so nothing here has to be taken on trust.

criteria.label: Original published work
criteria.body: Three open-source tools under permissive licences: a local CI gate, a dependency-free mock engine for third-party APIs, and an air-gapped automation platform. The first two ship with the harness that produced their measurements, so the performance claims can be independently reproduced.

criteria.label: Evidence of professional and technical competence
criteria.body: A published evidence document that shows how each number was taken, discloses the measurement that was discarded, and has a dedicated section listing the claims that are not made. A platform whose architecture is checkable by reading its layout rather than by trusting a benchmark.

criteria.label: Recognition beyond a single employer
criteria.body: A dated body of published writing spanning 2013 to 2026, addressed to working engineers rather than to an employer, plus live documentation sites and public repositories for each project.

criteria.label: Ongoing public activity
criteria.body: A continuous record of shipping and publishing, evidenced by the activity log and the commit history of each repository.

participation.policy: The adopter list is a file in the repository, and it grows by pull request. That makes it public, reviewable and impossible to inflate — a name on that list is a commit anyone can see and revert. Adding yourself takes a pull request and a row; there is no form, no email and no account.

mechanisms.title: Add yourself to the adopter list
mechanisms.body: Open a pull request against ADOPTERS.md adding a row: who you are, what you use the mocks for, and the year. That is the whole process. If you would rather not be listed, that is completely fine — the list exists for the people who want to be found.

mechanisms.title: Submit a mention, a talk or a write-up
mechanisms.body: Links to blog posts, talks, newsletters and social posts about a project belong in the community page's mentions table, and they are added by opening an issue with the URL. A link can be checked in one click, which is why the projects collect links rather than testimonials.

mechanisms.title: Contribute a mock as a file
mechanisms.body: The mock engine takes a contributed mock as a route file with no code in it, under contrib/. The test suite starts one, checks it answers, and fails if it does not — so a new provider is a small, reviewable pull request rather than a change to the engine.
